name: BI Tools & Dashboards
description: Building interactive business intelligence reports and dashboards with tools such as Power BI and Tableau, including data modeling and calculated measures.

questions.question: In a typical dashboard, what is a KPI card best used for?
options: Showing the full row-level detail of a table
Highlighting a single headline metric, often compared to a target
Displaying geographic distribution of sales
Editing the underlying data source
questions.explanation: A KPI (card) visual surfaces one key number, such as revenue this month, usually with a target or trend for context.

questions.question: In a star schema, which table typically holds numeric, transaction-level measurements such as sales amounts?
options: Dimension table
Lookup table
Bridge table
Fact table
questions.explanation: Fact tables store measurable events (amounts, quantities) and reference dimension tables that describe them (date, product, customer).

questions.question: In Power BI, what is the key difference between a calculated column and a measure?
options: A calculated column is computed row by row and stored in the model; a measure is evaluated at query time in the current filter context
A measure is stored in the model; a calculated column is evaluated only when a visual is rendered
Calculated columns can only contain text; measures can only contain numbers
There is no difference; the names are interchangeable
questions.explanation: Calculated columns are computed at refresh for each row and take memory; measures are aggregations computed dynamically based on filters and slicers.

questions.question: A slicer on a report page filters by Region. What does this let a viewer do?
options: Permanently delete rows for other regions from the dataset
Change the data type of the Region column
Interactively restrict the visuals on the page to the selected region(s)
Schedule a data refresh for one region only
questions.explanation: Slicers are on-canvas filters that change the filter context of visuals without modifying the underlying data.

questions.question: Which DAX expression returns total sales ignoring any filter applied to the Product table, e.g. for a percent-of-total calculation?
options: SUM(Sales[Amount])
CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), ALL(Product))
FILTER(Sales, Sales[Amount] > 0)
SUMX(Product, Product[Price])
questions.explanation: CALCULATE modifies the filter context, and ALL(Product) removes filters on the Product table, giving the grand total across products.

questions.question: What is row-level security (RLS) in a BI tool used for?
options: Encrypting the dataset file on disk
Speeding up visuals by caching rows
Preventing users from exporting a report to PDF
Restricting which rows of data each user or role can see in the same report
questions.explanation: RLS applies filters based on the viewer's identity or role, so e.g. a regional manager sees only their region's rows.

practical.title: Write a percent-of-total DAX measure
practical.instructions: A Power BI model has a Sales table with an Amount column and a Product table. Write a DAX measure named 'Sales % of Total' that divides the current total sales by total sales across all products. Use DIVIDE to avoid divide-by-zero errors.
practical.expected_output: Sales % of Total = DIVIDE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[Amount]), ALL(Product)))

rubric.hint: Use DIVIDE(numerator, denominator) rather than the / operator to handle zero safely.
Aggregate Sales[Amount] with SUM (or reference a total sales measure).

rubric.description: Uses CALCULATE to change filter context
rubric.hint: The denominator needs CALCULATE to modify the filter context.
Use ALL(Product) or REMOVEFILTERS(Product) inside CALCULATE to get the grand total.

tasks.title: Learn the Power BI basics
tasks.description: Work through Microsoft's Power BI getting-started documentation. Learn how to connect to a data source, use Power Query to shape data, and build your first report visuals.
tasks.completion_criteria: Can explain the difference between Power BI Desktop, the Power BI service, datasets and reports.

tasks.title: Build a one-page sales report
tasks.description: Import a sample sales CSV into Power BI or Tableau. Create a KPI card for total sales, a bar chart by category, a line chart over time and a region slicer.
tasks.completion_criteria: Report contains at least 4 visuals and a working slicer that filters all of them.

tasks.title: Model a star schema and write DAX measures
tasks.description: Split a flat dataset into a fact table and date, product and customer dimensions with relationships. Write measures for total sales, year-over-year growth and percent of total.
tasks.completion_criteria: Model has 1 fact and at least 3 dimension tables, and 3 working DAX measures used in visuals.

tasks.title: Publish an executive dashboard
tasks.description: Design a multi-page dashboard for a public dataset answering three business questions, with drill-through, tooltips and row-level security for at least one role. Publish it and gather feedback from a peer.
tasks.completion_criteria: Published dashboard with at least 2 pages, drill-through, an RLS role and a written summary of peer feedback.
